The GCD will give the largest number of bouquets such that each bouquet has the same number of white and red tulips.

First, factorize the numbers:
- 28 = 2² × 7
- 98 = 2 × 7²

The GCD is the product of the lowest powers of the common prime factors:
- Common prime factors are 2 and 7.
- Lowest power of 2 is 2¹.
- Lowest power of 7 is 7¹.

Thus, GCD(28, 98) = 2 × 7 = 14.

So, the greatest number of identical bouquets is 14. Each bouquet will have:
- White tulips per bouquet: 28 ÷ 14 = 2
- Red tulips per bouquet: 98 ÷ 14 = 7

This uses all the tulips with no leftovers.
